critiques.summary: H1 is adequately supported on every load-bearing hop and is the only hypothesis consistent with the evidence; the final round is closed with a confidence cap. Onset is pinned to the second: cert notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, metric bucket flip at 12:15, first error log 12:15:27Z (F2,F3,F4,F24,F25). The green-dashboard mechanism is directly evidenced — failures deferred as PENDING_RETRY on an async outbound rail, HTTP error_rate flat 0.16-0.28%, restarts=0, latency drops failing fast (F1,F4,F5). H1-vs-H2 separation rests on untruncated error text naming OUR client cert ('our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'; F25) with the 'remote error' prefix correctly resolved as where the alert was surfaced, not whose cert expired (F26,F30); the signature repeats 80x unchanged with zero alert-42/48 anywhere (F27,F28). All change-based alternatives are excluded by mechanism and path (F7,F13,F14,F15,F17); H2 survives only via permanent unobservability of the bank peer (F6,F16,F37, tc-016 failed) and would require a peer CA change coincidentally reproducing our exact notAfter. H2 is not provable either way, but it is not a peer-origin explanation positively evidenced — it is an unfalsifiable fallback, so it does not block acceptance. Remaining gaps are honesty issues, not blockers: cert notAfter comes only from runtime log text (no cert/secret inventory exists anywhere in the toolset — F19-F22,F38); the fleet sweep is incomplete (~6-8 services unqueried: market-data-service, notification-service, exchange-gateway, user-db, redis-cache, exchange-api, kyc-provider, email-provider), so 'confined to payment-service' is 8-of-many-verified; and no per-endpoint/per-pod/4xx-vs-5xx breakdown exists in the available metrics. None of these name a different origin or change the ranking.

No per-endpoint/per-pod/per-region or 4xx-vs-5xx breakdown was obtainable (metrics are aggregate-only), so '~97.5% of transfers fail' is inferred from aggregate bank_api_error_rate=100% and payment_success_rate~2.5% rather than proven per transfer type.
